tools.name: list_meetings
tools.description:
List meetings for the authenticated user.

Supports filtering by status, date range, participant, company, and room.
Returns paginated results with cursor-based navigation.
The search parameter performs keyword filtering (not semantic search).
Use expand to include related resources: "documents".

tools.name: list_upcoming_meetings
tools.description:
List the authenticated user's calendar events that have not ended.

Ordered by start time, with the meeting/VC URL and participant list needed to
build a brief or target a bot. A meeting already in progress is included and
comes first, so the earliest entry may have a start_time in the past — compare
start_time and end_time before calling it "the next meeting". within_hours bounds
how far ahead to look and defaults to the next 24 hours: an upcoming event must
start inside it, while a meeting already in progress is always listed however long
it runs. Raise it (max 168, a week) to reach further out. Paginated via cursor.

tools.name: get_meeting_transcript
tools.description:
Get the transcript of a meeting.

Takes a meeting ID (e.g. mtg_abc123) and returns speakers and
timestamped text segments.

tools.name: get_meeting_recording
tools.description:
Get a signed URL for a meeting recording.

Takes a meeting ID (e.g. mtg_abc123) and returns a temporary
download URL.

tools.name: schedule_meeting_bot
tools.description:
Schedule the AI note-taker bot to join a calendar event.

Takes a calendar event ID (e.g. evt_abc123 — obtain one from
list_upcoming_meetings; a recorded meeting's mtg_ id is not accepted).
Scheduling is asynchronous: the response acknowledges the request with
the event_id and status "scheduling".

tools.name: send_bot_to_meeting_url
tools.description:
Send the AI note-taker bot to a meeting link right now, with no calendar event needed.

Takes a Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Webex join link; the bot joins
immediately. For a meeting on the user's calendar, use schedule_meeting_bot instead.
Asynchronous: the response returns status "scheduling" and the meeting_id (mtg_...)
the recording and transcript will appear under; if the bot cannot be created, that
meeting never appears. If the user's note-taker is already scheduled for, joining, or in
that call (including one booked for a calendar event), it is kept and this meeting_id
will not resolve. Limited to 10 calls per minute and 60 per hour per user.

tools.name: cancel_meeting_bot
tools.description:
Cancel a previously scheduled note-taker bot for a calendar event.

Takes a calendar event ID (e.g. evt_abc123). Like scheduling,
cancellation is asynchronous: the response acknowledges the request with
the event_id and status "cancelling".

Only works while the meeting is still upcoming or in progress. Cancelling for a
meeting that has already ended is rejected, because removing its note-taker also
deletes the recording and transcript — so this is never the way to tidy up a past
meeting, and an evt_ id you cached earlier may no longer be cancellable.

tools.name: get_notetaker_automation
tools.description:
Get the note-taker automation level for the authenticated user.

The automation level is the standing policy deciding which calendar
events the bot joins on its own. Returns {"automation": <level>} where
level is one of JOIN_ALL_EVENTS, JOIN_AS_HOST, or MANUAL.

tools.name: set_notetaker_automation
tools.description:
Set the note-taker automation level for the authenticated user.

Takes one of JOIN_ALL_EVENTS (join every calendar event), JOIN_AS_HOST
(join only events the user hosts), or MANUAL (join only events scheduled
explicitly via schedule_meeting_bot). Returns the new {"automation": <level>}.

tools.name: list_rooms
tools.description:
List rooms for the authenticated user.

Rooms group related meetings together. Supports text search by title
and cursor-based pagination.
Use expand to include related resources: "documents", "meetings".

tools.name: get_document
tools.description:
Get a document by ID.

Takes a document ID (e.g. doc_abc123) and a format. Supported formats:
html, markdown, raw, docx, json. Defaults to markdown.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description:
Drain the authenticated user's event queue (e.g. meeting recaps becoming ready).

Returns the oldest available events and leases them with a visibility
timeout, so an immediate second call returns nothing. Pass ``event_type``
to lease only that type and leave every other type untouched for its own
consumer; omit it entirely to drain the whole queue — a blank type is an error,
not a wildcard.

Leaving ack=false is the reliable mode: the event reappears once its
visibility timeout lapses unless you ack it via ack_events, so nothing is
lost if handling fails. Passing ack=true retires events at pull time and
is therefore at-most-once — a dropped response loses that batch.

The envelope ``id`` identifies this queue row, not the thing that happened:
the same meeting can be announced twice (a redelivered dispatch, or a recap
regenerated with better content) and each arrives with a fresh ``id``. Key
your side effects on ``type`` plus an identifier inside ``payload`` so a
repeat *updates* what you already delivered instead of adding a second copy
— and treat the newer payload as authoritative rather than discarding it.

tools.name: ack_events
tools.description:
Acknowledge events so they are not redelivered.

Takes a list of event IDs (e.g. qev_abc123) returned by list_events.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: List all webhooks for the authenticated user.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description:
Create a new webhook.

Takes a URL, a list of event types to subscribe to, and an optional
enabled flag. Returns the created webhook including its secret.

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description:
Update an existing webhook.

Takes a webhook ID (e.g. whk_abc123) and any fields to update.
At least one field must be provided.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description:
Delete a webhook.

Takes a webhook ID (e.g. whk_abc123) and permanently removes it.
